/-!
# Szymanski's conjecture

Szymanski's conjecture states that every permutation on the $n$-dimensional doubly-directed
hypercube graph can be routed with edge-disjoint paths.

The doubly-directed hypercube is obtained from the hypercube graph $Q_n$ by replacing every edge
with two arcs, one in each direction. We model it using the undirected graph
`SimpleGraph.hypercube n`: a directed path in the doubly-directed hypercube is a path
(`SimpleGraph.Walk.IsPath`) in `hypercube n`, and the arcs it uses are its darts
(`SimpleGraph.Walk.darts`). Two paths use the same edge in the same direction exactly when they
share a dart, so the two opposite arcs of one edge may be used by two different paths.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Szymanski's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szymanski%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz89] Szymanski, T. H., *On the permutation capability of a circuit-switched hypercube*.
  Proc. Internat. Conf. on Parallel Processing (1989), 103-110.
- [Lu90] Lubiw, A., *Counterexample to a conjecture of Szymanski on hypercube routing*.
  Inform. Process. Lett. 35 (1990), 57-61.
- [BFH01] Baudon, O., Fertin, G., Havel, I., *Routing permutations and 2-1 routing requests in
  the hypercube*. Discrete Applied Mathematics 113 (2001), 43-58.
-/

@[category research open, AMS 5 68]
theorem szymanskis_conjecture (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n → Bool)) :
    ∃ p : (v : Fin n → Bool) → (hypercube n).Walk v (σ v),
      (∀ v, (p v).IsPath) ∧ ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (p u).darts.Disjoint (p v).darts := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Szymanski's conjecture.** Every permutation on the $n$-dimensional doubly-directed hypercube
graph can be routed with edge-disjoint paths. That is, if the permutation $\sigma$ matches each
vertex $v$ of the hypercube $Q_n$ to the vertex $\sigma(v)$, then for each $v$ there is a path in
$Q_n$ from $v$ to $\sigma(v)$ such that no two paths for two different vertices $u$ and $v$ use the
same edge in the same direction.

The paths need not be shortest paths: Lubiw [Lu90] showed that for $n \geq 5$ some permutations
cannot be routed by edge-disjoint shortest paths. A vertex fixed by $\sigma$ is routed by the
trivial path. The conjecture has been verified by computer for $n \leq 4$ [BFH01].

theorem szymanskis_conjecture_one (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : (v : Fin n → Bool) → (hypercube n).Walk v ((1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin n → Bool)) v),
      (∀ v, (p v).IsPath) ∧ ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (p u).darts.Disjoint (p v).darts :=

@[category test, AMS 5 68]
theorem szymanskis_conjecture_swap :
    ∃ p : (v : Fin 1 → Bool) →
      (hypercube 1).Walk v (Equiv.swap (fun _ => false) (fun _ => true) v),
      (∀ v, (p v).IsPath) ∧ ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (p u).darts.Disjoint (p v).darts := by
  have h : ∀ v : Fin 1 → Bool,
      (hypercube 1).Adj v (Equiv.swap (fun _ => false) (fun _ => true) v) := by
    simp only [hypercube_adj]
    decide
  refine ⟨fun v => Walk.cons (h v) Walk.nil, fun v => ?_, fun u v huv => ?_⟩
  · simp [Walk.cons_isPath_iff, (h v).ne]
  · simp [List.Disjoint, huv]

claims.decomposer_note: Universally quantified over all n and all permutations σ of the 2^n vertices (fixed points route trivially): for each vertex v there is a directed path v → σ(v) in the hypercube with each undirected edge replaced by two opposite arcs, such that no arc (edge in a given direction) is used by two different paths; paths need not be shortest (Lubiw 1990 shows shortest-path routing fails for n ≥ 5), and the reusable `SimpleGraph.hypercube` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib supplies the underlying undirected graph but the doubly-directed arc-disjointness must be encoded explicitly.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the mathematically identical proposition: for every n and every σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n → Bool), there is a family p v : (hypercube n).Walk v (σ v) with each p v an IsPath and (p u).darts disjoint from (p v).darts whenever u ≠ v. I verified this is faithful to the source: Mathlib's Dart is an ordered pair (Dart.ext_iff reduces equality to toProd), so dart-disjointness is exactly 'no two paths for different vertices use the same edge in the same direction', while opposite orientations of one edge are distinct darts and may both be used (doubly-directed). A directed path in the doubly-directed cube is precisely a walk in the undirected hypercube; IsPath matches the word 'paths' and is equivalent to allowing arbitrary walks (bypass shortens a walk to a path using a sublist of its darts). No shortest-path constraint is imposed (Lubiw 1990). Fixed points route by Walk.nil. n = 0 is trivially true, not vacuous. c05 was chosen as the base for its complete module/theorem docstrings with references and two proved category-test sanity checks (identity permutation; the Q_1 transposition, which exhibits two paths using the two opposite arcs of the same edge). Edits: binder renamed P → p, AMS tags made consistent, BFH01 reference added. c02's extra 'research solved' n ≤ 4 variant was not included since it lies outside the slot.

/-!
# Szymanski's conjecture

Szymanski's conjecture states that every permutation on the $n$-dimensional doubly-directed
hypercube graph can be routed with edge-disjoint paths.

The doubly-directed hypercube is obtained from the hypercube graph $Q_n$ by replacing every edge
with two arcs, one in each direction. We model it using the undirected graph
`SimpleGraph.hypercube n`: a directed path in the doubly-directed hypercube is a path
(`SimpleGraph.Walk.IsPath`) in `hypercube n`, and the arcs it uses are its darts
(`SimpleGraph.Walk.darts`). Two paths use the same edge in the same direction exactly when they
share a dart, so the two opposite arcs of one edge may be used by two different paths.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Szymanski's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szymanski%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz89] Szymanski, T. H., *On the permutation capability of a circuit-switched hypercube*.
  Proc. Internat. Conf. on Parallel Processing (1989), 103-110.
- [Lu90] Lubiw, A., *Counterexample to a conjecture of Szymanski on hypercube routing*.
  Inform. Process. Lett. 35 (1990), 57-61.
- [BFH01] Baudon, O., Fertin, G., Havel, I., *Routing permutations and 2-1 routing requests in
  the hypercube*. Discrete Applied Mathematics 113 (2001), 43-58.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace SzymanskisConjecture

/--
**Szymanski's conjecture.** Every permutation on the $n$-dimensional doubly-directed hypercube
graph can be routed with edge-disjoint paths. That is, if the permutation $\sigma$ matches each
vertex $v$ of the hypercube $Q_n$ to the vertex $\sigma(v)$, then for each $v$ there is a path in
$Q_n$ from $v$ to $\sigma(v)$ such that no two paths for two different vertices $u$ and $v$ use the
same edge in the same direction.

The paths need not be shortest paths: Lubiw [Lu90] showed that for $n \geq 5$ some permutations
cannot be routed by edge-disjoint shortest paths. A vertex fixed by $\sigma$ is routed by the
trivial path. The conjecture has been verified by computer for $n \leq 4$ [BFH01].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 68]
theorem szymanskis_conjecture (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n → Bool)) :
    ∃ p : (v : Fin n → Bool) → (hypercube n).Walk v (σ v),
      (∀ v, (p v).IsPath) ∧ ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (p u).darts.Disjoint (p v).darts := by
  sorry

/-- The identity permutation is routed by the trivial paths. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 68]
theorem szymanskis_conjecture_one (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p : (v : Fin n → Bool) → (hypercube n).Walk v ((1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin n → Bool)) v),
      (∀ v, (p v).IsPath) ∧ ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (p u).darts.Disjoint (p v).darts :=
  ⟨fun _ => Walk.nil, fun _ => Walk.IsPath.nil, fun _ _ _ => by simp⟩

/-- The transposition of the two vertices of $Q_1$ is routed by the two opposite arcs of its
unique edge. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 68]
theorem szymanskis_conjecture_swap :
    ∃ p : (v : Fin 1 → Bool) →
      (hypercube 1).Walk v (Equiv.swap (fun _ => false) (fun _ => true) v),
      (∀ v, (p v).IsPath) ∧ ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (p u).darts.Disjoint (p v).darts := by
  have h : ∀ v : Fin 1 → Bool,
      (hypercube 1).Adj v (Equiv.swap (fun _ => false) (fun _ => true) v) := by
    simp only [hypercube_adj]
    decide
  refine ⟨fun v => Walk.cons (h v) Walk.nil, fun v => ?_, fun u v huv => ?_⟩
  · simp [Walk.cons_isPath_iff, (h v).ne]
  · simp [List.Disjoint, huv]

end SzymanskisConjecture

items: Doubly-directed hypercube encoded via the undirected `SimpleGraph.hypercube n` (vertices `Fin n → Bool`) with arcs represented as `SimpleGraph.Dart`s; a directed path in the doubly-directed graph is a `Walk` in `hypercube n` with `IsPath`, and its arcs are `Walk.darts`.

Arc-disjointness is `(P u).darts.Disjoint (P v).darts` for all u ≠ v. Since darts are ordered pairs, two paths traversing the same edge in opposite directions are allowed, matching 'the same edge in the same direction' in the article.

Paths are required to be simple (`Walk.IsPath`), following the word 'paths'. This is equivalent to allowing arbitrary walks, since any walk can be shortened to a path using a subset of its darts; with `IsPath` a single path also cannot reuse a dart.
Fixed points of σ are routed by the trivial path `Walk.nil` (which satisfies `IsPath` and has no darts), as the decomposition notes require; the test theorem `szymanskis_conjecture_one` checks this.

Quantified over all n : ℕ including n = 0 (one vertex, only the identity permutation, trivially routable); no lower bound on n is imposed since the source states it for the n-dimensional hypercube in general.
Paths are not required to be shortest, per the article (Lubiw 1990 shows shortest-path routing fails for n ≥ 5); the docstring records this.

AMS tags 5 (combinatorics) and 68 (computer science, interconnection-network routing) on the main statement; two `@[category test]` theorems (identity permutation for all n, and the swap on Q_1 exercising that opposite arcs may both be used) are included as sanity checks of the encoding.

reviewer_notes: Source is terse; the Wikipedia article's own gloss ('no two paths for two different vertices use the same edge in the same direction') was used to fix the meaning of 'edge-disjoint' on the doubly-directed cube. No candidate omitted the slot and none raised objections to the decomposition; their unanimity plus direct inspection of Dart/Walk.darts/IsPath definitions gives high confidence. Only deliberate deviation from the slot text: two proved @[category test] theorems are included alongside the conjecture (repo convention for exercising an encoding); they are proved, so carry no faithfulness risk. Final file compiles with only the expected 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
